title: Resolve microbatch handshake deadlock causing TTFT and tokens/sec collapse across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Ava Chen
description: Production regression: multiple customers reported simultaneous increases in time-to-first-token (TTFT) and a sustained drop in tokens/sec across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments starting 2026-03-12 UTC. Root cause analysis shows a microbatch handshake deadlock between the request multiplexer and the kernel selector when multi-model fanout is active and KV cache prefetches are enabled. The deadlock manifests as long-running requests that hold multiplexer slots and prevent new microbatches from progressing, causing queue buildup and throughput collapse for affected models (notably long-context LLaMA-family variants).
reproduction_steps: Deploy model variant with KV prefetch enabled and multiplexing on a 4+ tenant host
Send concurrent mixed-size requests with 1-2 warm priming tokens followed by long generation sequences (context > 4096)
Observe microbatch coordinator log: repeated 'handshake wait' entries and kernel selector backpressure
Verify tokens/sec drop and TTFT spike in per-route dashboard and worker traces
investigation_findings: Race condition in microbatch handshake: coordinator waits indefinitely for kernel-ready ACK when kernel preemption handshake occurs during prefetch refill
Eviction of KV cache entries during fanout increased prefetch latency and exposed the race
Regression introduced with kernel-scheduling change in runtime-1.25.0 (merged PR #12098)
Issue reproducible in Hosted and Dedicated; Private customers with air-gapped kernel optimizations also hit the same path
Observed correlation with high multiplex ratios (>6) and frequent small priming requests
mitigation_plan: Immediate: deploy runtime-1.25.1-hotfix with handshake timeout (10s) that unlocks stuck microbatches and forces fallback to serial execution for the offending request
Rollback option: revert kernel-scheduling change (PR #12098) if hotfix shows regressions in lab runs
Increase prefetch buffer size for affected models as temporary workaround to reduce eviction frequency
Enable targeted canary on Dedicated pools and a small percentage (2%) of Hosted traffic before full rollout
Notify customers with affected models and provide temporary routing to compatible model variant where possible
rollout_plan: Cut hotfix branch and run full CI + stress tests against multiplex profiles (runtime-1.25.1-hotfix)
Deploy to Canary host group in Hosted region us-west-2 with enhanced telemetry
Monitor microbatch_handshake_latency, tokens/sec per-route, and queue depth for 1 hour; if stable, expand to Dedicated canaries
After 4-hour stable window, push to remaining Hosted clusters and then Dedicated; provide Private customers with patch bundle and upgrade instructions
Post-rollback play: if rollback required, set automatic traffic drain and trigger emergency rollback runbook
monitoring_and_metrics_changes: Add microbatch_handshake_latency histogram and alert when p99 > 3s
Add metric microbatch_deadlock_count incremented on handshake timeouts and tracked per model variant
Dashboard: TTFT by model-variant + tokens/sec by host + multiplex ratio heatmap
Synthetic test: run multiplex stress harness every 15m in staging and report regressions
